Framework target: HIPAA (Security Rule + Privacy Rule)

We are a regional telehealth platform ("ClearPath Health") that has been operating for 18 months. Our auditor arrives in 75 days. Below is our controls inventory as we have it today. Please produce the gap table and remediation memo.

---
ClearPath Health — Controls Inventory (self-assessed, October 2026)

CTL-01 | Unique user IDs | We assign unique usernames to every employee. HR onboarding form captures this. | Status: Implemented

CTL-02 | Automatic logoff | EHR vendor (AthenaHealth) enforces 15-minute session timeout on its platform. We have an email from our AthenaHealth rep confirming this setting is on. | Status: Implemented

CTL-03 | Encryption of PHI at rest | All PHI stored in AthenaHealth is encrypted. We rely on their SOC 2 report for this. We requested their latest report 3 weeks ago; it has not arrived yet. | Status: Implemented

CTL-04 | Workforce training | All employees complete HIPAA training at hire. Last completion records were in our old LMS which was decommissioned in March 2026. New LMS (Rippling) went live April 2026 but no training module has been built yet. | Status: Partial

CTL-05 | Business Associate Agreements | We have BAAs with AthenaHealth and our billing vendor (ClaimLogic). We recently added a cloud storage vendor (Backblaze) for backup files that may contain PHI. No BAA has been executed with Backblaze. | Status: Partial

CTL-06 | Risk analysis | We conducted a formal risk analysis in January 2025. The output was a Word document. No updates have been made since. | Status: Implemented

CTL-07 | Audit controls (activity logging) | Our IT admin says "we log everything" via Cloudwatch on our AWS environment. No log review procedure exists, no alerting policy is documented, and we have never produced a log review report. | Status: Implemented

CTL-08 | Contingency plan | We have a Business Continuity Plan template downloaded from a HIPAA consulting firm's website. It has not been customized, signed, or tested. | Status: Partial

CTL-09 | Physical safeguards — workstation use | We have a remote-first workforce. No written workstation use policy exists. Employees were verbally told not to work from public wifi. | Status: Implemented

CTL-10 | Transmission security | Our web application uses TLS 1.2. We have a screenshot of an SSL Labs test from February 2024. | Status: Implemented

---
Additional context: Our audit window covers April 2026 – March 2027. We are targeting HIPAA Security Rule compliance. The auditor is a third-party assessor our cyber insurer requires annually.

# ClearPath Health — HIPAA Security Rule Gap Table & Remediation Memo
## Internal Triage Document — Not an Auditor's Assurance Opinion

---

## ARTIFACT 1: Per-Control Gap Table

| Control ID | Framework Mapping | Control Statement | Status | Evidence Required to Close | Gap Type | Vendor-Dependent? | Risk Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CTL-01 | §164.312(a)(2)(i) — Unique User Identification (required) | Unique usernames assigned at hire via HR onboarding form | **Partial** | (1) HR onboarding form itself (dated artifact showing ID-assignment process); (2) a current user roster or IdP export demonstrating unique IDs across the full workforce population — not just new hires; (3) evidence that terminated employee IDs are disabled (provisioning/deprovisioning procedure or ticket log, within audit window Apr 2026–Mar 2027) | doc + process | No | P2 |
| CTL-02 | §164.312(a)(2)(iii) — Automatic Logoff (addressable) | AthenaHealth enforces 15-min session timeout per vendor email | **Partial** | (1) A dated configuration screenshot or vendor-produced admin console export (not a rep's email) confirming the timeout setting is active as of a date within the audit window; (2) if ClearPath has any systems outside AthenaHealth that handle PHI (e.g., internal admin tools, email with PHI), those must be addressed separately; (3) documented policy or procedure referencing the addressable spec and the compensating rationale if any | doc + vendor | Yes (AthenaHealth config evidence) | P2 |
| CTL-03 | §164.312(a)(2)(iv) / §164.312(e)(2)(ii) — Encryption at Rest (addressable); also §164.308(b)(1) — BAA requirement for subprocessors | Relying on AthenaHealth SOC 2 for encryption assertion; report requested but not received | **Missing** | (1) AthenaHealth SOC 2 Type II report covering a period that overlaps with the audit window (Apr 2026–Mar 2027); (2) review documentation showing ClearPath assessed the report's encryption controls as relevant; (3) documented policy identifying what PHI is held where and which controls apply — encryption cannot be asserted by reference to a report that has not been received | vendor + doc | Yes (AthenaHealth SOC 2 not in hand) | P1 |
| CTL-04 | §164.308(a)(5)(i) — Security Awareness and Training Program (required) | Hire-time HIPAA training; prior LMS decommissioned Mar 2026; new LMS has no training module | **Missing** | (1) A training module built and launched in Rippling LMS covering required HIPAA Security Rule topics (form: completion records per employee); (2) completion records for all current workforce members within the audit window (Apr 2026–Mar 2027) — prior records in decommissioned LMS are unavailable and do not satisfy the current window; (3) a documented training program policy with cadence (annual minimum) and scope (all workforce including contractors with PHI access) | process + tooling (module build) | No | P1 |
| CTL-05 (a) | §164.308(b)(1) / §164.314(a)(1) — Business Associate Agreements (required) | BAA gap: Backblaze (cloud backup with PHI) has no executed BAA | **Missing** | (1) Executed BAA with Backblaze covering PHI stored in backup files, signed by authorized parties, dated before any PHI transfer to Backblaze; (2) inventory of all vendors/subprocessors that receive or store PHI and confirmation each has an executed BAA (not draft, not 'in progress') | vendor + doc | Yes (Backblaze must countersign) | P1 |
| CTL-05 (b) | §164.308(b)(1) / §164.314(a)(1) | Existing BAAs with AthenaHealth and ClaimLogic | **Implemented** | Executed BAAs confirmed to exist for both vendors. No gap to close, but recommend annual review to confirm BAA terms remain current when either vendor updates its services. | — | No | P3 (housekeeping note) |
| CTL-06 | §164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) — Risk Analysis (required) | Risk analysis conducted Jan 2025; no updates since | **Partial** | (1) The Jan 2025 risk analysis document itself — confirm it is dated, scoped to all ePHI systems (including AthenaHealth, Backblaze, AWS environment, and any others added since Jan 2025), and signed by an accountable owner; (2) a risk analysis update or re-assessment that incorporates system changes since Jan 2025 (Rippling LMS, Backblaze onboarding, decommissioned old LMS) — HIPAA requires the analysis to be kept current and reasonably up to date; (3) a risk management plan or remediation log showing that identified risks are being tracked to closure | doc + process | No | P1 |
| CTL-07 | §164.312(b) — Audit Controls (required) | AWS CloudWatch logs exist; no review procedure, no alerting policy, no review reports | **Partial** | (1) A documented audit control policy or procedure specifying which events are logged, review frequency, who performs review, and escalation path (form: written procedure); (2) evidence that logs span all systems that store or transmit ePHI — not just AWS (must include AthenaHealth-side events to the extent accessible via CUEC); (3) at minimum one completed log review record within the audit window (Apr 2026–Mar 2027) showing dates, reviewer, and disposition of any anomalies | doc + process | No | P1 |
| CTL-08 | §164.308(a)(7)(i) — Contingency Plan (required); §164.308(a)(7)(ii)(A–E) — sub-specifications | Downloaded BCP template; not customized, signed, or tested | **Missing** | Template downloaded from a third-party consulting firm with no adoption indicators is not an adopted policy artifact — this is Missing, not Partial. Required to close: (1) ClearPath-specific contingency plan covering data backup plan, disaster recovery plan, emergency mode operations, testing and revision procedures, and applications/data criticality analysis (all required sub-specs under §164.308(a)(7)); (2) evidence of at least one tabletop or functional test within the audit window with documented results and any follow-up actions; (3) plan must bear an adoption date, approval signature, and ClearPath branding/scope | doc + process | No | P1 |
| CTL-09 | §164.310(b) — Workstation Use (required); §164.310(c) — Workstation Security (required) | No written workstation use policy; verbal guidance only for remote workforce | **Missing** | (1) Written workstation use policy covering permitted locations, screen privacy requirements, acceptable use on personal devices if applicable, and encryption requirements for endpoint storage — verbal guidance does not satisfy the written-policy requirement; (2) for a remote-first workforce, the policy should address home network security requirements and public wifi prohibition with specifics; (3) evidence the policy was distributed to all workforce members and acknowledged (e.g., signed acknowledgment form or LMS completion record) within the audit window | doc | No | P1 |
| CTL-10 | §164.312(e)(1) — Transmission Security (required); §164.312(e)(2)(ii) — Encryption (addressable) | TLS 1.2 in use; SSL Labs screenshot from February 2024 | **Partial** | The Feb 2024 SSL Labs screenshot is outside the audit window (Apr 2026–Mar 2027) — a 32-month-old screenshot does not demonstrate current configuration. Required to close: (1) A current SSL Labs or equivalent scan dated within the audit window showing TLS version, cipher suite configuration, and certificate validity; (2) a documented transmission security policy or standard referencing minimum TLS version and applicable systems; (3) if any PHI is transmitted via email or non-browser channels, those channels must be addressed separately | doc + process | No | P2 |

**Note on CTL-08:** The unadopted consulting template qualifies as Missing (not Partial) because a template with no adoption date, no signatures, and no internal customization does not demonstrate a control is in place — it is equivalent to no artifact.

---

## ARTIFACT 2: Remediation Memo

**TO:** ClearPath Health Leadership (CISO / Head of Compliance / CEO)
**FROM:** Compliance Gap Analysis — Internal Triage
**DATE:** October 2026
**RE:** HIPAA Security Rule Readiness — 75 Days to Assessor Arrival
**CLASSIFICATION:** Internal Use Only — Not an Assurance Opinion

---

### Executive Summary

ClearPath Health has 75 days before its cyber-insurer-required HIPAA assessment. Of 10 control areas reviewed (one split into two sub-items), **zero qualify as fully Implemented with audit-ready evidence**, **one is Implemented** (existing BAAs with AthenaHealth and ClaimLogic), **four are Partial**, and **five are Missing** — including the unadopted contingency plan and the absent Backblaze BAA. The program has **six P1 likely-findings** as currently evidenced: missing risk analysis update, no operating audit-log review program, no workforce training records in the current window, missing Backblaze BAA, unadopted contingency plan, and the undelivered AthenaHealth SOC 2 report underlying the encryption assertion. **ClearPath is not ready for a HIPAA assessment in 75 days without immediate action on all P1 items.** One control (CTL-08, contingency plan) cannot realistically be closed in 75 days if a live tabletop test is required — this should be discussed with the assessor regarding scope or timing. The Backblaze BAA is vendor-dependent and must be initiated this week.

---

### P1 Gaps — Must Close Before Assessment

**P1-A | CTL-03 — AthenaHealth SOC 2 Report Not in Hand (Encryption / Subprocessor reliance)**
- Gap: ClearPath is asserting encryption compliance by reference to a report it has not received. Assessors will ask to see the report.
- Owner: **Procurement or Vendor Management lead** — escalate outstanding request to AthenaHealth account executive immediately; set 10-day deadline.
- Gap type: Vendor
- Bucket: **30 days** (report must be in hand; if AthenaHealth cannot deliver, document compensating controls or consider alternative evidence)
- Note: Also requires a documented review memo confirming ClearPath assessed the report's relevant controls.

**P1-B | CTL-04 — No HIPAA Training Records in Current Audit Window**
- Gap: Old LMS decommissioned; new LMS has no training module. No workforce has completed training in the Apr 2026–Mar 2027 window.
- Owner: **HR / People Operations lead** (module build and launch); **IT Operations** (Rippling LMS configuration)
- Gap type: Process + Tooling (module build)
- Bucket: **30 days** for module launch and initial completions; **60 days** for full workforce completion with records exported
- Note: Every day this is delayed reduces the amount of evidence accrual before the assessment.

**P1-C | CTL-05 (a) — No BAA with Backblaze**
- Gap: PHI is flowing to Backblaze backup storage with no executed BAA. This is a per se HIPAA violation under §164.308(b)(1), not merely a documentation gap.
- Owner: **Legal / General Counsel** (BAA negotiation and execution); **Procurement** (vendor contact)
- Gap type: Vendor + Doc
- Bucket: **Immediate** — PHI transfer to Backblaze should be suspended until a BAA is executed, or legal must assess risk tolerance. Target execution within 15 days.

**P1-D | CTL-06 — Risk Analysis Stale; Not Updated for Material System Changes**
- Gap: Jan 2025 analysis is 21 months old. HIPAA requires the risk analysis be updated when the environment changes — ClearPath has added Backblaze, changed LMS platforms, and decommissioned systems since then.
- Owner: **CISO or equivalent / Security Engineering lead**
- Gap type: Doc + Process
- Bucket: **30 days** for updated risk analysis draft covering all current ePHI systems; **45 days** for final sign-off and accompanying risk management plan

**P1-E | CTL-07 — Audit Controls Exist But No Review Program**
- Gap: CloudWatch logs are present, but raw log capture is not a HIPAA audit control until someone reviews them. No procedure, no review records, no alerting.
- Owner: **IT Operations / Security Engineering lead**
- Gap type: Doc + Process
- Bucket: **30 days** for written log review procedure; **45 days** for first documented review cycle with anomaly disposition

**P1-F | CTL-08 — Contingency Plan Is an Unadopted Template**
- Gap: The downloaded template is not an adopted policy. ClearPath effectively has no contingency plan on record. All five required sub-specifications (backup, DR, emergency mode ops, testing, criticality analysis) are open.
- Owner: **IT Operations / CISO** (drafting); **CEO or COO** (approval and sign-off)
- Gap type: Doc + Process
- Bucket: **30 days** for draft customized to ClearPath's environment; **60 days** for adoption and sign-off; **75 days** for tabletop test — **this is extremely tight**. If the assessor requires evidence of a completed test cycle, recommend discussing scope accommodation or a post-assessment remediation plan with the assessor before fieldwork begins.

**P1-G | CTL-09 — No Written Workstation Use Policy**
- Gap: Verbal instruction does not satisfy HIPAA's written-policy requirement for §164.310(b)/(c). For a fully remote workforce this is a visible gap.
- Owner: **IT Operations / HR** (drafting and distribution); **CISO** (approval)
- Gap type: Doc
- Bucket: **14 days** — this is purely documentation-closeable; writing the policy should be the fastest P1 to close. Include workforce acknowledgment collection.

---

### P2 Gaps — Close or Have Remediation Plan Ready

**P2-A | CTL-01 — Unique User ID (Process Partially Documented)**
- Gap: HR onboarding form addresses new hire ID assignment but no evidence of deprovisioning process or full workforce roster.
- Owner: **IT Operations / HR jointly**
- Gap type: Doc + Process
- Bucket: **45 days** — produce a user roster export and a written deprovisioning procedure with at least one example of a termination ticket processed during the audit window.

**P2-B | CTL-02 — Session Timeout Evidence Is Vendor-Provided Email (Insufficient)**
- Gap: A vendor rep's email is not a configuration artifact. Assessors want to see the actual setting.
- Owner: **IT Operations** (obtain admin console screenshot or vendor-produced config report); **Vendor Management** (coordinate with AthenaHealth)
- Gap type: Vendor + Doc
- Bucket: **30 days** — request config export or admin panel screenshot from AthenaHealth alongside the SOC 2 request.

**P2-C | CTL-10 — TLS Evidence Out of Date (32-Month-Old Screenshot)**
- Gap: Feb 2024 screenshot predates the audit window. Easy to re-run.
- Owner: **Security Engineering / IT Operations**
- Gap type: Doc
- Bucket: **7 days** — re-run SSL Labs or equivalent; document result with date; attach to a transmission security policy stub.

---

### P3 Gaps — Housekeeping

**P3-A | CTL-05(b) — AthenaHealth and ClaimLogic BAAs (Implemented, Annual Review Recommended)**
- Confirm BAA terms are still current given any service changes in the past 12 months. Low risk but a common assessor question.
- Owner: **Legal**
- Bucket: **90 days** (before next annual review)

---

### Vendor-Dependent Items — Procurement Must Act This Week

| Item | Dependency | Status | Action Required | Realistic Timeline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CTL-03 | AthenaHealth SOC 2 Type II report | Requested; not received | Escalate to AthenaHealth AE; set 10-day deadline; document if delayed | 2–4 weeks |
| CTL-05(a) | Backblaze BAA execution | Not initiated | Legal to send BAA immediately; suspend PHI transfer until executed | 1–3 weeks (depends on Backblaze legal response time) |
| CTL-02 | AthenaHealth session timeout config evidence | Email only; no config artifact | Request admin console export alongside SOC 2 request | 2–3 weeks |

Vendor items cannot be closed by internal work alone. Assign a named point of contact at each vendor and set hard deadlines with escalation paths. Do not allow these to sit in a procurement queue.

---

### Recommended Sequencing

**This week (Days 1–7):**
1. Suspend PHI transfer to Backblaze until BAA is signed (Legal decision required Day 1).
2. Escalate AthenaHealth SOC 2 and session-timeout config evidence requests to account executive level.
3. Re-run SSL Labs scan — this is a 20-minute task (CTL-10).
4. Assign CISO or equivalent as risk analysis owner and schedule kickoff (CTL-06).
5. Draft workstation use policy — documentation-only, should be done in 5–7 days (CTL-09).

**Days 8–30:**
6. Launch HIPAA training module in Rippling; collect completions for all current workforce (CTL-04) — every week of delay is a week less evidence.
7. Write audit log review procedure and complete first review cycle (CTL-07).
8. Begin ClearPath-specific contingency plan draft (CTL-08) — this has the longest process lead time.
9. Finalize and sign updated risk analysis (CTL-06).
10. Produce workforce user roster and deprovisioning procedure (CTL-01).

**Days 31–75:**
11. Full workforce HIPAA training completion with records exported (CTL-04).
12. Contingency plan signed, tabletop test scheduled — **if tabletop cannot be completed before fieldwork, discuss scope with assessor now, not later** (CTL-08).
13. Second log review cycle documented (CTL-07 — one cycle may not satisfy assessor; two is stronger).
14. Review and finalize AthenaHealth and ClaimLogic BAA currency (CTL-05b).

**Honest assessment:** With 75 days and six P1 findings, ClearPath can realistically close most gaps if work starts immediately. The contingency plan testing timeline is the highest risk of being incomplete at fieldwork. Recommend a pre-assessment call with the assessor to surface this proactively rather than having it emerge during fieldwork.

*This document is an internal triage analysis and does not constitute legal advice, a HIPAA compliance determination, or an auditor's assurance opinion.*

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response correctly identify the Feb 2024 SSL Labs screenshot as outside the Apr 2026 audit window (Missing/Partial, not Implemented), classify the unadopted consulting template as Missing rather than Partial, and catch that the AthenaHealth SOC 2 not-yet-received means CTL-03 is Missing? These three temporal and adoption traps are the core discrimination test — a generic template cannot produce the correct calls without reading the planted dates.
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Does the gap table have specific, actionable evidence requirements (form + scope + period) for each control, with correct HIPAA section citations (§164.308, §164.310, §164.312)? Does the memo give an honest 'not ready' verdict with P1 items clearly distinguished and the contingency plan flagged as realistically uncloseable within 75 days?
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response correctly handle CTL-08 (unadopted template = Missing, not Partial) differently from CTL-04 (process + tooling gap) and CTL-09 (doc-only gap), showing it reads each control's specific situation rather than applying a single pattern?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Are HIPAA citations correct (§164.312(b) for audit controls, §164.308(a)(7) for contingency plan sub-specs, §164.308(b)(1) for BAAs)? Does the response correctly identify that the Backblaze situation is a per se compliance issue (PHI in flight to a non-BAA vendor), not just a documentation gap?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the executive summary clear about the 75-day constraint and the honest 'not ready' verdict without burying the message in compliance jargon? Does the memo separate vendor-dependent items actionably?

metadata.judge_notes: Three planted traps require scenario-specific reasoning: (1) CTL-10's SSL Labs screenshot is from Feb 2024, which is BEFORE the Apr 2026 audit window — the correct classification is Partial/Missing, not Implemented; a generic template will miss this. (2) CTL-08's BCP template has no adoption indicators — it is Missing, not Partial; 'Partial' is the trap answer for anything with any artifact present. (3) CTL-03 is Missing because the SOC 2 report hasn't been received — 'in progress' requests don't count as evidence. The response should also catch that CTL-05(a) (Backblaze) is a P1 and potentially a live compliance violation, not just a documentation gap. Penalize any response that marks CTL-10 Implemented, CTL-08 Partial, or CTL-03 Implemented/Partial without noting the report is absent.

# Meridian Analytics — ISO 27001:2022 Gap Table & Remediation Memo
## Internal Triage Document — Not a Certification Body Opinion

---

## ARTIFACT 1: Per-Control Gap Table

| Control ID | ISO 27001:2022 Annex A Mapping | Control Statement | Status | Evidence Required to Close | Gap Type | Vendor-Dependent? | Risk Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| INT-01 | A.5.1 — Policies for information security | InfoSec Policy v2.1, approved by CEO October 2024 | **Partial** | The policy exists and is dated — however, October 2024 is 24 months before the February 2027 audit. ISO 27001 requires periodic review; most certification bodies expect at least annual review. Evidence to close: (1) a re-review and re-approval of the policy dated within 12 months of audit fieldwork (i.e., no earlier than February 2026) — ideally October 2026 or later; (2) documented review record showing who reviewed it, what changed (or was confirmed unchanged), and re-approval with CEO or delegated ISMS owner signature | doc | No | P2 |
| INT-02 | A.8.2 — Privileged access rights; A.8.18 — Use of privileged utility programs (2022 revision) | AWS IAM least-privilege roles set up 14 months ago; no subsequent review | **Partial** | Role configuration may be sound, but ISO 27001 A.8.2 requires periodic review of privileged access rights. Evidence to close: (1) a documented procedure for periodic IAM role review (frequency defined — typically quarterly or semi-annual for privileged roles); (2) at minimum one completed review cycle within the audit window, documented with date, reviewer identity, and disposition of any over-provisioned roles found; (3) evidence that the role definitions were applied consistently across all AWS accounts in scope (not just the account the engineer worked in initially) | doc + process | No | P1 |
| INT-03 | A.8.28 — Secure coding; A.6.3 — Information security awareness, education and training (2022 revision) | Secure coding checklist in Notion; 3/8 developers have viewed it; no training | **Partial** | Three coverage problems: (a) no training has been delivered — a document is not a training program; (b) 5 of 8 developers have no evidence of exposure to the checklist at all; (c) no evidence the checklist reflects current threat landscape (2 years old). Evidence to close: (1) a training session or structured review covering the checklist, with attendance records for all 8 developers, delivered within the audit window; (2) an updated checklist with a review/approval date; (3) a documented secure development policy or procedure that formalizes the checklist's use in the SDLC, not just its existence in Notion | doc + process | No | P1 |
| INT-04 | A.5.19 — Information security in supplier relationships; A.5.20 — Addressing information security within supplier agreements; A.5.21 — Managing information security in the ICT supply chain | AWS as primary supplier; shared responsibility model reviewed; no formal assessment or register | **Partial** | Reviewing AWS's shared responsibility model documentation is not a supplier security assessment. Evidence to close: (1) a supplier/vendor register listing all suppliers in scope (AWS and any others — CI/CD tools, monitoring, etc.) with risk classification; (2) a documented supplier security assessment process — typically a questionnaire or structured review against security criteria (for AWS, this may reference AWS's SOC 2 / ISO 27001 reports as the assessment artifact, but must be documented as such with a review memo); (3) a supplier agreement or addendum addressing security requirements, or documentation that AWS's standard terms were reviewed and accepted as sufficient for the risk level | doc + process | Partial (AWS attestations exist; documenting their review is internal work) | P2 |
| INT-05 | A.5.24 — Information security incident management planning and preparation; A.5.26 — Response to information security incidents; A.5.28 — Collection of evidence | Documented IR policy Mar 2026; no tabletop or real incident | **Partial** | The policy (IR-POL-001, Mar 2026) is a genuine dated artifact — this is not Missing. However, ISO 27001 requires evidence of the incident management process operating, not just documented. Evidence to close: (1) at least one tabletop exercise conducted within the audit window with documented scenario, participants, outcomes, and any follow-up action items; (2) evidence that the IR policy was communicated to relevant staff (distribution record or training record); (3) confirm IR-POL-001 covers all required sub-elements (detection, classification, escalation, containment, recovery, post-incident review, evidence preservation) | process | No | P2 |
| INT-06 | A.8.8 — Management of technical vulnerabilities (2022 revision) | Dependabot running; no formal policy, no SLA, no review records | **Partial** | Dependabot is a tooling capability, not a vulnerability management program. Evidence to close: (1) a documented vulnerability management policy or procedure specifying scope (all repos, all environments), severity classification, remediation SLAs by severity, and responsible owner; (2) records showing Dependabot alerts were reviewed and dispositioned within the current audit window — export of closed/resolved alerts with dates and disposition notes; (3) evidence that critical/high severity alerts are tracked to closure within defined SLA | doc + process | No | P1 |
| INT-07 | A.8.24 — Use of cryptography; A.8.5 — Secure authentication (partially) | AWS RDS encryption confirmed by Aug 2026 console screenshot; no encryption policy or key management procedure | **Partial** | The console screenshot is a genuine artifact within the audit window — encryption at rest appears to be operating. However, A.8.24 requires a policy on cryptography use, not just evidence of one tool's encryption setting. Evidence to close: (1) a cryptography policy covering: which data classifications require encryption, approved algorithms and key lengths, key management lifecycle (generation, rotation, revocation), and who is responsible; (2) confirmation that encryption covers all data stores in scope — the screenshot addresses RDS but are backups, S3 buckets, or EBS volumes also encrypted? Scope must be demonstrated; (3) evidence of key rotation schedule or confirmation AWS-managed keys are used with documented acceptance | doc | No | P2 |
| INT-08 | A.7.1–A.7.13 — Physical controls (2022 revision) | Fully remote; no physical offices; all infrastructure in AWS | **Implemented** | For a fully remote organization with no owned or leased physical premises and infrastructure solely in AWS, Annex A physical controls (A.7.x) are either not applicable or addressed through AWS's physical security controls (covered by AWS's ISO 27001 / SOC 2 certifications).
